bridges.statement: Religious patterns disclose enduring structures of reality and experience that should continue to guide contemporary life.
Scripture principally expresses participatory patterns of identity, action, and lived experience rather than failed mechanical science.
People reason from within inherited stories, so legitimate reform is organic, goal-directed, and enacted by participants rather than from an imagined neutral exterior.
Christianity orders inevitable hierarchy through love, compassion, and humanization while distinguishing enduring patterns from particular behavioral applications.
Inherited religious patterns should guide contemporary life only after scrutiny shows that they remain accurate and adaptive in present environments.
Recurring religious motifs are non-arbitrary products of evolved human psychology rather than independent evidence of divine or permanently normative structures.
Shared evolved consciousness and explicit goals provide a sufficiently deep standpoint for comparing mutually incompatible traditions and revising them.
Religious claims and prescriptions should be compared with evidence, other traditions, and present consequences so useful motifs can be retained and harmful ones removed.
Dogmatic authority and obsolete religious prescriptions can preserve tribal harms and deny people legitimate forms of contemporary life.
